objective: maximize note revenue by combining useful free acquisition articles with paid conversion articles, while measuring the free-to-paid funnel without speculative optimization

internalEvidence.interpretation: First-party article-level funnel metrics are not yet available. Do not claim a winning theme, CTA uplift or optimal price until equal-age 24h/72h/7d evidence exists.

findings: Use reactions to free articles as demand signals rather than assuming paid-only publishing is optimal.
Cross-link closely related free and paid articles to increase qualified circulation and purchase opportunities.
Strong paid-article free areas commonly contain empathy or question framing, a concrete change/example, and a clear statement of reader benefit.
Free portions and free articles should remain useful on their own rather than acting as thin teasers.

paid.rule: Do not reduce or replace this floor with free articles. Reader-visible URL, exact title, expected price, paid boundary and dedicated cover are still required before a paid publication counts.

initialExperiment.note: 2/day is an experimental starting cadence, not a proven optimum. Do not raise cadence before comparable funnel evidence exists.

contentRules: Every free article must provide standalone practical value.
Do not publish thin teaser-only posts.
Use at most one context-matched paid CTA per free article.
Only insert a paid URL after that URL has been independently reader-visible verified; never guess URLs.

Prefer problem diagnosis, checklists, mistakes, quick wins, frameworks and small worked examples for free articles; reserve deeper implementation systems, templates, full workflows and reusable assets for paid articles.

funnelArchitecture.ctaRule: Place one related paid CTA after the useful free core. No unrelated multi-product CTA stack.
funnelArchitecture.reverseLinkRule: Paid articles may link back to useful free companion articles when this improves context or series discovery.
paidFreeAreaRule: Open with empathy, a practical question or a recognizable problem.
Show a concrete change, worked example or before/after so the buyer can evaluate relevance.
State the specific value the paid section adds beyond the free area.
Keep enough standalone value in the free area for a reader to judge quality before purchase.

comparisonRules: Do not compare raw lifetime PV between articles of different ages; compare matched post-publication windows.
Keep article-level observations separate from theme-level conclusions until multiple articles support the same pattern.
Do not infer clicks or purchases from public availability, likes or PV.
Use medians within the same age window when enough articles exist; avoid declaring winners from a single noisy observation.

testOrder: free article to paid article theme/intention match
specific incremental value added by the paid article
diagnosisMatrix.rule: Change one major variable at a time where possible and preserve a rollback baseline.
Do not blame CTA or price before acquisition is sufficient to evaluate them.

diagnosisMatrix.action: Create adjacent-intent free satellite articles that independently solve nearby problems and point to the verified paid article with one relevant CTA.

diagnosisMatrix.condition: free article strong and paid click-through strong but purchase weak
free and paid response both weak after sufficient exposure
diagnosisMatrix.action: Deprioritize the theme rather than cloning title variants.

experimentGuardrails.priceChangeRule: Do not make a large price change without observed demand/conversion evidence or a strong market-based reason.
experimentGuardrails.ctaChangeRule: Only use a reader-visible verified destination and never add more than one paid CTA to a free article by default.

currentState.actionNow: Do not churn CTA, price or publication cadence before the first comparable 24h evidence becomes available. Prepare measurement and keep future paid free areas compliant with the three-element qualification gate.
